records.title: Prague Metro D
records.answer: Prague's fourth metro line is under construction in stages. The first independently operable section is planned between Pankrác and Nové Dvory; construction contracts, renamed stations, monitoring and temporary street access each describe a different part of its delivery.
records.scope: One Metro D railway project across the defined I.D1, I.D2 and I.D3 stages, not the existing metro network. Individual stations, construction lots, monitoring contracts and adjacent development do not create extra counted projects; proposed branches beyond this scope are not admitted here.
records.stage: The first section has been under construction since April 2022; the next section began work in June 2026. The June account forecasts Pankrác–Nové Dvory operation in the second half of 2032. November traffic notices describe upcoming restrictions, not completed works or passenger opening.

identity_decision.rationale: Count Prague Metro D once as the named staged railway. Preserve the I.D1 operating subset and I.D2/I.D3 extensions without counting each station or construction contract again. Prague is a separately bounded municipal place; its tram, housing and utility examples remain contextual systems rather than further project additions in this group.

timeline.event: Construction began on Pankrác–Olbrachtova, as recalled in the June 2026 account.
DPP reported signing the next-section construction contract.
Ceremony marked the next section; the release says initial works began that week.
Council approved Nusle and Ryšánka as replacements for working station names.
The rolling progress page reports access-tunnel excavation and associated monitoring starting at Nové Dvory.
DPP published future traffic arrangements and distinguished passage completion from opening.

sections.heading: A staged railway with changing station names
sections.text: Metro D's defined stages connect the southern districts with Pankrác and ultimately Náměstí Míru. The project description identifies a five-station initial operating section to Nové Dvory, a southern continuation toward Písnice and a northern continuation beyond Pankrác. These are stages of one railway, not independent additions to the project count. Council's August 31 decision changed the working name Olbrachtova to Ryšánka and Náměstí Bratří Synků to Nusle. The final name of the station provisionally called Depo Písnice remained deferred. Preserving both old and new names makes earlier contracts intelligible without mistaking a renamed station for a new asset.

sections.heading: A signed construction lot is not the whole line
sections.text: DPP's April 7 account reports signing the Olbrachtova–Nové Dvory construction contract for CZK 29.99 billion excluding VAT. That is the specified lot's tender price, not final expenditure for all of Metro D. The June 19 ceremony followed the start of initial work that week; it did not mark passenger operation. The June release expects the shortest independently operable section, Pankrác–Nové Dvory, to open in the second half of 2032. Its five stations need to function together. Construction progress in one part therefore cannot establish completion of the railway or delivery of the full northern and southern extensions.

sections.heading: Systems scope needs its own contract evidence
sections.text: The June construction announcement describes tunnels, stations and technology installation, but its two language versions differ on a consequential detail. The Czech release excludes transport and control systems from one description of the installation scope; the English release includes them. The announcement alone cannot settle the contractual boundary for those systems. Keeping that conflict visible matters because civil works, train supply, control equipment and integrated testing have to meet at commissioning. A tunnel can advance while another delivery package follows a different procurement sequence. The actual signed scope and interface requirements are the appropriate next evidence, not a preferred translation.

sections.heading: Excavation depends on monitoring the surrounding ground
sections.text: The rolling next-section account reports September access-tunnel excavation at Nové Dvory and the accompanying start of geotechnical monitoring. It describes building-condition surveys, measurement points and evaluation of deformation, tilt and forces as work progresses. Surveys are phased around the construction schedule rather than treated as permanently valid records for every building. This is a practical connection between underground work and the people living above it: a baseline and repeated measurements make changes traceable. The described monitoring process is not an independent finding that no damage has occurred. Its interpretation needs location, timing, thresholds and any response to an observed change.

sections.heading: Street access changes before the railway opens
sections.text: The November 10 notice schedules Sulická's closure from November 25, 2026 to June 30, 2027, coordinating metro utility diversions with water and sewer replacement. Bus diversions and temporary road connections are part of maintaining access around those works. They were future arrangements at the November 22 inspection, not an observed journey. The same notice distinguishes expected December completion of a Pankrác passage section from full public opening with Metro D. Residents can therefore encounter a completed structure that is not yet a usable connection. Street restoration, construction completion and passenger access need separate dates and clearly explained dependencies.

sections.heading: Evidence test from construction to usable service
sections.text: Editorial evidence test: follow each construction and systems package through its actual scope, interface tests, acceptance and entry into service. Preserve renamed-station mappings so later records can be compared with earlier contracts. Connect ground-monitoring results to thresholds and corrective actions without publishing unnecessary property details. For the surrounding neighbourhoods, compare announced diversions with actual duration and accessible routes to homes, hospitals and existing transport. At opening, assess the whole journey through entrances, transfers and train service. These records would distinguish an advancing construction program from a dependable railway while keeping future extensions outside the initial service denominator.

next_artifacts: Signed systems-scope and interface records resolving the Czech/English announcement conflict.
Dated package acceptance, integrated testing and passenger-opening decisions.
Scoped geotechnical observations, thresholds and documented responses.
Actual closure, restoration and accessible-transfer records for surrounding streets.

records.title: Prague municipal services
records.answer: Prague's municipal services connect transport expansion with water treatment, housing support and district-level childcare. The city-wide account needs to retain the different boundaries of treatment lines, referral-based housing and individual neighbourhood projects.
records.scope: One capital-city municipality of Prague, not the surrounding Central Bohemian region or the entire Prague Integrated Transport catchment. Prague 5 childcare and Nové Dvory illustrate services within the city; neither adds another place or project identity here.
records.stage: November wastewater information distinguishes the July transfer between treatment lines. Housing and childcare pages describe access arrangements, while Nové Dvory design work and the October tram start concern future provision. These are not universal service coverage or a combined municipal performance score.

identity_decision.rationale: Count Prague once as the capital-city municipality, separate from the Metro D railway. District examples retain their local scope without being counted as additional municipalities. Regional transit coverage, shared utility networks and proposed mixed-use buildings do not extend the place boundary or create extra portfolio identities in this account.

timeline.event: The Nové Dvory account dates approval of the area planning study to this month.
PDS reports signing key design and project-management contracts for Project 1.
PVK's table identifies a limit change associated with the old-line shutdown and transfer to the new line.
DPP marked the start of the Libuš–Nové Dvory tram construction.
PVK updated the wastewater quality table, retaining different reporting periods for the two lines.

sections.heading: Wastewater results need the right treatment boundary
sections.text: PVK's November 9 update shows June figures for the old central treatment line and October figures for the new line. It explains a July 1 change in discharge limits associated with shutting the old line for reconstruction and transferring wastewater to the new one. That operational change matters when comparing results: the two tables do not describe identical months or unchanged treatment scopes. The page also distinguishes monthly figures, cumulative averages and limits assessed on an annual-average basis. They should not be collapsed into one city-wide compliance verdict. Prague's branch treatment plants likewise remain distinct from the central facility.

sections.heading: Rental support depends on referral and available homes
sections.text: The Municipal Rental Agency describes a route into housing through partner social workers, housing contact points and other referral services when capacity is available. It does not accept direct applications or maintain its own applicant queue. For people offered a suitable home, it describes a standard one-year tenancy with possible renewal, technical help and support in establishing payments or managing unexpected income difficulties. This connects a dwelling to the conditions needed to keep living there. Referral is not a guaranteed offer or a promised waiting time, and a renewable contract is not an indefinite tenancy. The capacity constraint belongs beside the service description.

sections.heading: Childcare is delivered at district scale
sections.text: Prague 5 describes three children's groups operated through its social and nursing-care centre. Their listed capacities are twenty-two, twenty-two and ten children, with different age bands rather than one interchangeable pool of places. The groups serve younger children before kindergarten and the page provides an application route for the 2026/27 year. For families, the age match and location are part of whether care is usable alongside work and travel. Listed capacity is not a count of vacancies or a city-wide childcare entitlement. These three groups illustrate one district's provision; they cannot represent every neighbourhood or establish an individual admission.

sections.heading: Nové Dvory links land use to a future station
sections.text: PDS's Project 1 places two mixed-use blocks beside the future Nové Dvory metro station, with planned connections to its vestibules. The proposed uses include housing, commerce, offices, cultural space and parking. The account separates the September 2022 planning study, key design and management contracts signed in 2025, and preparation continuing in 2026. This sequence explains how a station and its surrounding neighbourhood are being coordinated. It is not occupied housing or completed public premises. The interfaces matter as much as the building outlines: residents will need entrances, public space and useful connections that become available with the relevant phases.

sections.heading: A tram extension also moves water infrastructure
sections.text: The October 7 start of the 1.8-kilometre Libuš–Nové Dvory tram extension joins transport construction to another basic service. DPP expects substantial time to be spent relocating Želivka water mains and coordinating with Metro D works. Its late-2028 trial-operation date is a forecast. The tram work also prepares foundations for a future passage to Libuš metro station, but that passage is intended to open with the station, not simply when its foundations exist. This phased arrangement avoids treating every visible piece of infrastructure as immediately usable and shows why transport, water continuity and neighbourhood access have to be planned together.

sections.heading: Evidence test for connected municipal delivery
sections.text: Editorial evidence test: track water performance across the treatment change with explicit sampling periods and operating boundaries. For housing, follow referrals through offers, move-in and sustained tenancy, retaining the reasons an eligible household may not receive a home. For childcare, separate listed capacity, places offered, attendance and the needs of different age groups. Follow Nové Dvory's buildings and transport connections through their own acceptance and opening dates. These measures would show whether coordinated planning produces usable services in particular neighbourhoods without substituting one flagship construction milestone for the experience of residents across the city.

next_artifacts: Comparable treatment-period records and correctly scoped regulatory assessments.
Referral, offer and tenancy-retention outcomes with clear population denominators.
District childcare capacity, admission and attendance records by age group.
Building, tram, water-main and accessible-passage handovers with separate opening dates.

records.title: Brno municipal services
records.answer: Brno's municipal account connects heat production and distribution, flood-stage preparation, district-managed housing and public-transport maintenance. Reported equipment delivery, trial results and application rules each need their own outcome and service-access evidence.
records.scope: One statutory city of Brno, not the whole South Moravian region, river basin or utility catchment. Named heat sources, river stages, depots and district housing offices are service examples within the place account, not additional counted projects or municipalities.
records.stage: October's heat-source presentation reports earlier trial operation; November's river account retains contractor selection and preparation stages. Municipal housing access is district-managed, while transport reports describe delivered maintenance equipment and winter preparation rather than observed winter-wide reliability.

identity_decision.rationale: Count Brno once within its municipal boundary. Keep heat supply chains, river-basin dependencies and regional travel as context without expanding that boundary. Brno-sever, the Trnitá flood stages and Medlánky depot illustrate local systems; none is separately added to the project inventory in this group, and individual city districts do not add place counts.

timeline.event: The municipal housing page dates the common application form's introduction to this day.
The heat company described steam-to-hot-water network reconstruction in named streets.
DPMB reported completion of the Medlánky lathe and wash-line investments.
The heat company presented Brno-sever and reported the preceding heating season's trial results.
The city reported a grant decision for Trnitá flood-protection stages, with contractor selection continuing.
DPMB described preparations for the coming winter.
The city described preparation, tree measures and future main works along the rivers.

sections.heading: Trial heat production and annual potential differ
sections.text: Teplárny Brno's October 1 presentation of the modernized Brno-sever source reports about 3,000 trial operating hours during the 2025/26 heating season. It attributes roughly 15,000 tonnes of avoided carbon dioxide to comparison with gas production during that trial. The separate figure of up to 38,000 tonnes annually concerns full-use potential, not an already measured annual result. The plant combines heat and electricity production and receives wood chips by rail through the municipal forestry company's supply arrangement. Those dependencies matter for continued operation. The operator's gas comparison is not an independent lifecycle assessment or proof that the fuel chain is carbon-neutral.

sections.heading: Heat must also reach the buildings
sections.text: The heat company's April account describes replacing steam pipes with hot-water distribution in several streets, including Špitálka, Štěpánská, Přízová, Nádražní and Benešova. The stated aims are lower heat losses, operating costs and emissions. These network works are distinct from installing a new generating source: useful heat must pass through distribution and building interfaces before it serves a household. The notice does not quantify realized whole-network savings or establish that every street intervention has finished. A lower-loss design also does not, by itself, determine each resident's bill. Delivery dates and measured distribution performance need to accompany the production account.

sections.heading: Flood protection advances through separate river stages
sections.text: The city's October account reports a CZK 1.815 billion grant decision for Trnitá stages IX–XI while contractor selection continues. November's preparation account distinguishes those future works from completed Poříčí stages. The next works aim to provide more room for the Svratka and Svitava through reshaped banks, channels and floodplain features, alongside public access. Their tree program includes planned transplanting and replacement planting as well as clearance. A grant decision is not accepted construction, and a planting plan is not tree survival. The proposed protection standard also retains its river-specific design assumptions rather than promising the elimination of all flood risk.

sections.heading: A common housing form does not create one allocation queue
sections.text: Brno's municipal housing information describes a common application form introduced on January 1, 2026, which can be sent to more than one district. The districts still manage ordinary municipal homes, set published selection criteria and choose tenants. A shared form can reduce repeated administrative work without making the allocation systems identical. Some districts have no ordinary municipal rental stock, and registration is not an offer of a vacant home. The official indexed text was available after direct retrieval timed out; it supports the published process, not a live vacancy check. No application or individual eligibility assessment was carried out.

sections.heading: Reliable transport needs workshop and winter routines
sections.text: DPMB's May account reports completed Medlánky investments in a mobile wheel lathe and renewed tram wash line. The lathe can service wheels without removing them and is intended to shorten the time a vehicle spends unavailable. A separate November account describes heating checks, ice-prevention equipment and preparations for keeping vehicles and switches usable in winter. These are concrete maintenance arrangements, not a measured guarantee that every trip will run. The distinction links workshop capacity to the street: faster repair may support service availability, but actual vehicle downtime, cancellations and accessible journeys are the outcomes residents experience.

sections.heading: Evidence test for municipal service outcomes
sections.text: Editorial evidence test: compare actual heat production and distribution losses with their stated periods, fuel assumptions and delivered quantities. Keep trial comparisons apart from annual forecasts and follow the supply chain as well as the plant. For river works, preserve grant, procurement, acceptance and maintenance dates, then assess protection and ecological outcomes within the relevant design conditions. Track housing applications through district decisions and sustained occupation, and connect transport maintenance to observed service reliability. These separate records would make progress and uneven access visible without turning one investment announcement into a city-wide verdict.

next_artifacts: Heat and electricity operating results, fuel-chain evidence and separately measured distribution losses.
Flood-stage procurement, acceptance, maintenance and ecological-survival records.
District housing application, allocation and tenancy-retention outcomes.
Vehicle downtime, cancellations and accessible-service results over a defined winter period.
